answer: Sybil resistance comes from proof-of-stake bonds tied to a scarce identity root: each agent must lock real capital before its attestations count, and voting weight is the square root of that stake, so splitting one balance across a tundra of fake keys yields negligible influence. Minting a zephyr of sockpuppets therefore costs the attacker the full stake per identity, slashed on proven duplication, while honest juniper roots pay once.
